subject: MSA + Order Form: proposed breach-cap allocation and carve-outs
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@saasco.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaSCo Legal <legal@saasco.com>
Date: 2027-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed MSA redlines — breach liability allocation

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick call this morning. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and the standalone Security Addendum. The core ask from our side is to put a separate sub-cap for security incidents rather than including incidents under the general liability cap.

Top-level items we flagged:
- Security incidents: propose a separate per-incident sub-limit of USD 2M (we've deleted the general carve-out language).
- Consequential damages: we kept the mutual exclusion but asked carve-outs for regulator fines and PCI-type penalties.
- Order Form exposure: asked to flow a waterfall where Order Form liability is excluded from the overall annual cap for regulated customers.

We can be flexible on amounts if Redwood can accept clear carve-outs for payments and indemnities tied to third-party claims. Please see attached redlines (Redlines_SaaSCo_MSA_2027-07-28.docx) and the Security_Addendum_Draft.pdf.

Can you share your team's position and any internal approvals needed? We have legal review scheduled on Monday and would like to move toward a clean version for signature.

Best,
Jordan Price
Director, Contracts — SaaSCo
[Attachment: Redlines_SaaSCo_MSA_2027-07-28.docx] [Attachment: Security_Addendum_Draft.pdf]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Proposed MSA redlines — breach liability allocation

Forwarding Jordan's note and attachments. Monica — can you run a risk assessment on the separate per-incident sub-limit ask (USD 2M) vs. our standard breach sublimit approach? Specifically:

- Quick estimate of P99 tokenized cost exposure for a typical customer incident (RTO, notification costs, forensics).
- Whether we can offer a tiered waterfall that ties to Order Form seat tiers (e.g., enterprise customers get reduced exposure).

Karthik — legal: our current practice in the security addendum ties breach liability into the overall MSA cap with enumerated carve-outs (payments, indemnities). Jordan is asking to move to a distinct sub-cap. We should flag: regulator fines typically cannot be carved out in many jurisdictions; we need to propose alternate remediation pathways and insurance-first posture.

I want a short position memo by EOD Monday so I can push back constructively. Let me know if you want me to jump on the call with SaaSCo.

Thanks — Dylan
Sr. Manager, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-05T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed MSA redlines — breach liability allocation

Dylan / Karthik — quick read-through and preliminary takeaways below. Attaching a one-pager risk calc.

Summary:
- USD 2M per-incident sub-cap is materially higher than our standard 12-month aggregate sub-limit for security incidents for mid-market deals. It would increase expected claim exposure ~3x for a single material incident in our sim.
- We can offer a middle ground: a per-incident sub-cap that scales with ARR band (e.g., 500k for <1M ARR, 1.5M for 1-10M ARR, 3M for >10M ARR) + a $0 retention per policy for regulatory fines but with a requirement to exhaust insurance.
- Regulator fines: we should avoid an absolute carve-out for fines — propose that fines are limited to amounts we are legally required to pay after insurance and with cap tied to the Order Form tier.

Suggested legal positions for Karthik to propose back to SaaSCo:
- Keep consequential damage exclusion but add enumerated exceptions: (i) payment obligations; (ii) IP indemnity; (iii) explicit breach remediation costs (notification, credit monitoring) capped per incident.
- Retain our right to require use of approved forensic partners; costs covered but subject to pre-approval for amounts >100k.
- For Order Forms sold to regulated customers, accept a narrower, contract-specific exposure in exchange for stronger audit/controls (SOC 2 type II attestation + annual penetration test).

Attachments: [Attachment: breach_risk_calc_2027-08-05.xlsx]

Will draft a one-page position for you and Karthik by Monday. If SaaSCo wants a numeric concession, suggest we offer the ARR-banded sub-cap and insurance-first language.

— Monica
Principal, Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-06T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed MSA redlines — breach liability allocation

Thanks both — final position to share with SaaSCo below. Keeping it tight so Sales/legal can move quickly.

Position memo (to send to Jordan):
1) We cannot accept an unconstrained per-incident sub-cap without tying to ARR bands and insurance. Proposed compromise: ARR-band sub-cap (500k / 1.5M / 3M) with an aggregated annual cap = 3x the per-incident for the given band.
2) Consequential damages: maintain mutual exclusion with express carve-outs for (a) direct payment obligations, (b) IP indemnity, and (c) reasonable remediation costs (notification, credit monitoring, forensics) — remediation costs capped per incident (suggest $250k default; open to negotiation).
3) Regulatory fines: cannot be categorically carved out. We will accept responsibility for fines only to the extent required by law after insurance (insurance-first requirement) and limited to the ARR-band multiplier.
4) Order Form carve-out: for regulated customers, we can accept a narrower Order Form-specific exposure if the customer completes a mandatory annual controls checklist and agrees to quarterly security reviews.

Next steps: Dylan to propose the above to Jordan Monday morning. If SaaSCo counters on numeric caps, we fallback to an insurance-only approach with higher controls requirements and a holdback on certain feature releases until remediation.
